essence: Photographing the same evening view helped Nia Moss notice how differently a shaded wall and a sunlit sky changed colour.
brief: Moss photographed one east-window view for a fortnight and kept the camera settings fixed. A wall in shade often appeared blue while the clouds still held sunlight. Written notes helped record differences between the camera’s image and what Moss remembered seeing.
understanding: Keeping the viewpoint fixed allowed Moss to notice the changing relationship between surfaces as evening light fell across them.
The method paired fixed exposure and white balance with cloud-cover notes and a written visual impression. The wall and clouds sometimes appeared to belong to different hours.
A sensor and an eye respond differently, and the observations concern a single view. Moss used the disagreement as part of the record rather than treating the image as a definitive account of colour.
